$comment: ★★★ <direct.h> on pe declares its own surface and includes nothing else — the references' graph. DSS's shipped surface for a target is the platform references' surface (P68 round 9, the coordinator's ruling of 2026-09-23 on D-CONFIG-SYS-STAT-OVER-DECLARES-S-ISLNK-ON-PE, option (a)): a declared superset deviation must not be used to meet a HARNESS need — what a harness needs, it supplies as shims handed to BOTH compilers — or a program built with DSS on Windows fails with every Windows reference. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: `#include <direct.h>` + a `DIR *` and `readdir` is rc=1 under mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and rc=2 under MSVC 14.51 (`/std:clatest`), against an `_mkdir` control on the same header that is rc=0 on both — neither reference reaches `DIR` from <direct.h>, so a program that wants the directory API includes <dirent.h>, as it must with mingw. Until that ruling this descriptor carried `includes: [{header: dirent.h, when: {format: pe}}]` (LANE-CFG edit 3/4), a declared superset deviation taken so sqlite's `ext/misc/fileio.c` — which on the mingw path includes <direct.h> and its own `_MSC_VER`-gated, inert `windirent.h`, never <dirent.h> — would compile; its measured cost was that a pe TU including <direct.h> could no longer define its own complete `struct DIR` (F_ShippedTypeIdentityConflict). `examples/c/pe_direct_dirent_superset` and tests/analysis/preprocess/test_platform_header_surface pin the reference graph. | ★ TF-C111 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION P3): `library.pe` is now ucrtbase.dll — moved with the whole co-state group (malloc/stdlib/string/stdio/io/errno/direct/process/sys-stat in ONE commit). Membership is `_getcwd`/`_wgetcwd`: passed a NULL buffer they ALLOCATE the result on the CRT heap for the caller to free, and they set errno on failure — both runtime-owned identities. All 8 symbols re-MEASURED as ucrtbase exports at TF-C111 (`objdump -p`); no renames were needed, and the msvcrt dumpbin ordinals quoted below are retained as the c98 provenance record, NOT as the current binding. | Neutral shipped <direct.h> (Microsoft CRT directory management) — c98 (Windows-host sub-arc, the 3-header F001A batch). shell.c includes it on the pe route in the fileio extension (the `#else` of its !_WIN32 guard), whose mkdir macro routes to fileio_mkdir -> `_wmkdir(b1)`: of the eight names this descriptor ships, `_wmkdir` is the one the generated shell.c and sqlite3.c spell (✔MEASURED 2026-09-24, sqlite f544d3599a10, a word search for each name). The remaining seven ship as the obviously-paired trivial siblings: the narrow/wide couples of the classic direct.h set (_mkdir/_wmkdir, _rmdir/_wrmdir, _chdir/_wchdir, _getcwd/_wgetcwd) — _getcwd doubles as the corpus example's live-run witness (a cwd read needs no argv, which pe lacks until D-RUNTIME-PE-MAIN-ARGS). `availableObjectFormats:[pe]` — a Microsoft-CRT header fails loud on elf/macho. `library:{pe:msvcrt.dll}` — all eight are msvcrt.dll exports (verified via dumpbin /exports: _chdir 209, _getcwd 368, _mkdir 658, _rmdir 695, _wchdir 911, _wgetcwd 985, _wmkdir 995, _wrmdir 1012), NOT kernel32. SIGNATURES (Microsoft SDK direct.h/corecrt_wdirect.h): char* _getcwd(char*,int) — note the int maxlen (POSIX getcwd takes size_t; the CRT form is i32) and the char* return (the buffer, or NULL); int _mkdir(const char*) — NO mode param (unlike POSIX mkdir(path,mode); sqlite's mkdir macro drops the mode for exactly this reason); int _rmdir(const char*); int _chdir(const char*); the wide forms take/return wchar_t* — Windows wchar_t is UTF-16 u16 (== windows.json's WCHAR), so they spell ptr<u16> (same stddef.json wchar_t=i32 latent-width note as io.json).
